question: The Commission’s Secretariat-General recently announced its intention to set up a European intelligence agency. However, intelligence does not fall within any of the Commission’s exclusive or shared competences. It falls under ‘national security and defence’ and directly affects the sovereignty of the Member States. Consequently, the EU is not supposed to take the place of the Member States in this area.

To respond to the threats facing Europe, the EU already has structures in place to facilitate cooperation between national agencies (Club de Berne, Europol, Frontex and the EU Intelligence and Situation Centre). 1.

Did the Member States instruct the Commission to take this initiative, or were they consulted beforehand? If not, why does the Commission believe that it has the authority to propose the creation of such a structure?
As guardian of the Treaties, does the Commission recognise that respect for the division of powers laid down by the Treaties is an integral component of the rule of law?
Why is it considering setting up a new structure when the existing bodies already liaise with the national intelligence services?
